# SPD-082 — Give the resume its own event kind member.resumed: migration 0003, kernel.EVENT_KINDS, and the six user_version assertions it moves

## Brief
SPD-050 makes a resumed spudagent count as live again, but the resume rides on the member.started event (data resumed/was_stopped_at/cleared) instead of a kind of its own, because a new kind reaches four files and four test modules no member of wave 1 owns. Giving it the kind would make spud events --kind member.resumed work, keep member.started meaning "a member started", and let the SubagentStop hold key on a kind rather than a data flag. It is cosmetic, not correctness: everything SPD-050 asked for works today.

Evidence: The work, all of it known and mechanical. (1) bin/spudlib/state/schema.py: a DDL_0003 that rebuilds the events table with member.resumed added to the kind CHECK, exactly as DDL_0002 did for the seven project and session kinds (SQLite cannot alter a CHECK); MIGRATIONS gains it and SCHEMA_VERSION = len(MIGRATIONS) becomes 3. (2) bin/spudlib/core/kernel.py line 44 EVENT_KINDS gains the string, which cli/cliparser.py line 314 turns into the --kind choices. (3) bin/spudlib/hooks/recording.py: RESUME_KIND, at the top of the resume comment block, flips from "member.started" to "member.resumed"; nothing else in recording.py or subagent_stop.py changes, since last_resume already queries by RESUME_KIND, and the resume then needs its own event beside the plain member.started rather than replacing it. (4) the version assertions move from 2 to 3: tests/test_init.py line 32 (SCHEMA = 2), tests/test_backup.py lines 99 and 202, tests/test_migrate_projects.py lines 86 and 173 (applied and user_version, and the fixture at line 58 that migrates from 1), tests/test_hooks.py line 5128. (5) tests/test_hooks_resume.py asserts the kind of the resume event, which is written against RESUME_KIND rather than a literal. Operationally: the merge of a SCHEMA_VERSION bump makes every spud command refuse until spud migrate runs, so it wants a quiet moment rather than the middle of an eleven-ticket batch.
